geometry_edits.rationale: Open the wing separation a bit more so the court becomes a clearer public figure.
Keep a continuous ground-contact bar to anchor the public threshold on the street edge.
Broaden the base to make the lower mass read as a usable plinth rather than a thin connector.
Increase the void slightly so the courtyard has stronger public presence and section relief.

graph_edits.rationale: Retain the dominant split-wing gesture but smooth the fragmentation into a more continuous sectional rule.
Preserve the active ground edge as a legible public threshold.
Strengthen the grounded base so the open court reads as supported public space rather than a mere notch.
Slightly enlarge the public court to improve usability and daylight while keeping the wrapped mass compact.

rationale: The candidate reads coherently across the four views as one courtyard-centered massing idea: a compact perimeter-like body split into wings around a public void, with the parcel boundary respected and the access edge answered by a legible opening rather than a sealed frontage. The dominant gesture is clear, and the open-space figure is strong. The main weakness is the silhouette: the stepped/fragmented roof and vertical excisions are readable but not especially resolved as a single capacity-bearing section, so the form lands closer to a competent early mass than a fully articulated sectional scheme. Programmatically it can plausibly support neighborhood living / mixed-use because it offers an active ground threshold, one clear public void, and a hierarchical upper mass without becoming an arbitrary object.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: More tower-like and vertically emphatic than this low courtyard composition; do not copy the silhouette as-is.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Stepped/tapered upper mass with a compact base and a clear skyline hierarchy; useful for keeping a dominant body while varying the top.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Office-tower typology and height logic are not a direct match for neighborhood living.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Single strong mass with a softened/torqued profile; suggests how one dominant volume can remain legible while being subtly deformed.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Its object-like sign/tower element is not necessary here and would be too literal if copied.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Grounded, low street-facing mass with a clear public edge and adjacent taller marker element; good precedent for active frontage plus compact vertical accent.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Much larger and more complex than the candidate; use the void logic, not the scale or full urban composition.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Courtyard/public void as organizing figure, with mass wrapped around an inhabited open space and a continuous ground relationship.
